components.note: 離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 他很小就离家去外地工作了。
example.pinyin: Tā hěn xiǎo jiù líjiā qù wàidì gōngzuò le.
example.english: He left home to work elsewhere when he was very young.
example.fact: The United Nations estimated that about 281 million people were living outside their country of birth as international migrants in 2020. A large share left home primarily in search of better economic opportunity, joining family members already abroad, or fleeing conflict. That figure has grown steadily for decades as global travel and communication have made moving away from home more feasible.

examples.hanzi: 他十八岁就离家去了北京。
examples.pinyin: Tā shíbā suì jiù líjiā qùle Běijīng.
examples.english: He left home for Beijing at eighteen.

examples.hanzi: 离家这么久,我特别想妈妈做的菜。
examples.pinyin: Líjiā zhème jiǔ, wǒ tèbié xiǎng māma zuò de cài.
examples.english: After being away from home so long, I really miss Mom's cooking.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — calling and speech: 吗, 喊, 呼; 叫 is to shout.
丩 (jiū) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 纠 jiū.
酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks: 酒, 醉 drunk, 酸 sour; 醒 is sobering up, then waking.
星 (xīng) sounds exactly like 醒 (tone differs).

example.hanzi: 请明天早上七点叫醒我。
example.pinyin: Qǐng míngtiān zǎoshang qī diǎn jiàoxǐng wǒ.
example.english: Please wake me up at seven tomorrow morning.
example.fact: The snooze button was introduced on alarm clocks in the 1950s, and Westclox's 1956 'Drowse' model set the nine-minute snooze interval that became an industry standard. The odd length was reportedly chosen because of gear-ratio constraints inside the clock's mechanism rather than any particular psychological reasoning. That same nine-minute default still shows up on many digital alarm clocks and smartphones today.

examples.hanzi: 闹钟响了,你快把弟弟叫醒。
examples.pinyin: Nàozhōng xiǎng le, nǐ kuài bǎ dìdi jiàoxǐng.
examples.english: The alarm has gone off, so go wake up your younger brother.

examples.hanzi: 一阵雷声把我从梦里叫醒了。
examples.pinyin: Yí zhèn léishēng bǎ wǒ cóng mèng lǐ jiàoxǐng le.
examples.english: A peal of thunder woke me from my dream.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 演出的开场非常精彩。
example.pinyin: Yǎnchū de kāichǎng fēicháng jīngcǎi.
example.english: The opening of the show was spectacular.
example.fact: Cirque du Soleil, founded in Quebec in 1984, transformed circus performance by removing traditional animal acts entirely and building shows instead around narrative-driven acrobatics and original music. Its opening acts were designed to immediately immerse audiences in a specific theme or story, a sharp departure from the traditional ringmaster-led circus format. The approach helped the company grow from a small Canadian troupe into a global entertainment brand.

examples.hanzi: 这场电影的开场很吸引人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng diànyǐng de kāichǎng hěn xīyǐn rén.
examples.english: The opening of this movie is very engaging.

examples.hanzi: 演唱会晚上七点开场,别迟到。
examples.pinyin: Yǎnchànghuì wǎnshang qī diǎn kāichǎng, bié chídào.
examples.english: The concert starts at seven in the evening, so don't be late.

components.note: 车 (vehicle) — the spokes of a cartwheel; also in 轮 wheel, 辆 for cars.
畐 (fú) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 福 fú and 幅 fú.
身 (body, bow) — 身 is a worn-down picture of a bow, with a hand 寸 drawing it — 射 is to shoot.

example.hanzi: 医生提醒他要小心辐射。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng tíxǐng tā yào xiǎoxīn fúshè.
example.english: The doctor reminded him to be careful of radiation.
example.fact: Marie Curie, who discovered the properties of radioactivity alongside her husband Pierre in the late 1890s, died in 1934 of aplastic anemia almost certainly caused by decades of radiation exposure. Her personal notebooks remain so radioactive that they are stored today in lead-lined boxes at France's national library, and visitors who wish to view them must sign a waiver and wear protective clothing.

examples.hanzi: 手机的辐射对身体影响不大。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī de fúshè duì shēntǐ yǐngxiǎng bú dà.
examples.english: Phone radiation has little effect on the body.

examples.hanzi: 太阳光向四周辐射热量。
examples.pinyin: Tàiyángguāng xiàng sìzhōu fúshè rèliàng.
examples.english: Sunlight radiates heat in all directions.

components.note: 钅 (metal; traditional 金) — marks metals, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron, 铜 copper; 铺 is a shop or a spread-out bed; once metal tiles on a door.
甫 (fǔ) — close sound: 铺 pū. 甫 also sounds out 捕 bǔ, 哺 bǔ and 辅 fǔ.

example.hanzi: 请帮我把床铺好。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ chuáng pū hǎo.
example.english: Please help me make the bed.
example.fact: 铺 is pū as a verb (铺床 make a bed, 铺路 pave a road, 铺垫 lay groundwork) and pù as a noun for a shop or bed: 店铺, 床铺. 铺张 means extravagant.

examples.hanzi: 她在桌子上铺了一块白布。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhuōzi shàng pū le yí kuài báibù.
examples.english: She spread a white cloth over the table.

examples.hanzi: 工人们正在铺路。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài pūlù.
examples.english: The workers are paving the road.

components.note: 冫 (ice) — marks cold and reduction, as in 冰, 冷, 冻; 减 is to lessen.
咸 (xián) hints at the sound: 减 jiǎn is close to 感 gǎn, 喊 hǎn and 碱 jiǎn.

example.hanzi: 我想减肥，所以少吃甜食。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jiǎnféi, suǒyǐ shǎo chī tiánshí.
example.english: I want to lose weight, so I eat less sweets.
example.fact: 减 is the opposite of 加: 减少 (to reduce), 减肥 (to lose weight), 减价 (price cut), 减速 (to slow down), and 减法 (subtraction). 加减乘除 are the four arithmetic operations.

examples.hanzi: 你的体重减了多少？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ de tǐzhòng jiǎn le duōshao?
examples.english: How much weight have you lost?

examples.hanzi: 十减三等于七。
examples.pinyin: Shí jiǎn sān děngyú qī.
examples.english: Ten minus three equals seven.

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
艹 (grass, plants) — plants and leaves: 花, 草, 叶; 落 is leaves falling.
洛 (luò) sounds exactly like 落; related to 各 gè in 路 lù.

example.hanzi: 警方仍未查明失踪者的下落。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng réng wèi chámíng shīzōngzhě de xiàluò.
example.english: The police still haven't determined the missing person's whereabouts.
example.fact: Amelia Earhart disappeared over the Pacific Ocean in July 1937 while attempting to become the first woman to fly around the world. Despite numerous search expeditions in the decades since, including several well-funded modern efforts using sonar and underwater robots, her aircraft's final resting place has never been conclusively confirmed.

examples.hanzi: 我的钱包不知下落,可能丢在出租车上了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de qiánbāo bù zhī xiàluò, kěnéng diū zài chūzūchē shàng le.
examples.english: I don't know where my wallet is; maybe I left it in the taxi.

examples.hanzi: 飞机的高度在快速下落。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī de gāodù zài kuàisù xiàluò.
examples.english: The plane's altitude is dropping rapidly.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and leaves: 花, 草, 叶; 落 is leaves falling.
洛 (luò) sounds exactly like 落; related to 各 gè in 路 lù.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 这个地区的经济发展相对落后。
example.pinyin: Zhège dìqū de jīngjì fāzhǎn xiāngduì luòhòu.
example.english: This region's economic development is relatively backward.
example.fact: Bhutan formally adopted a 'Gross National Happiness' framework into its constitution in 2008, using it alongside or instead of GDP to measure national progress. The index weighs factors such as psychological well-being, health, education, and environmental conservation rather than economic output alone. The approach has drawn international attention as an alternative way to think about what counts as development.

examples.hanzi: 他在班上的成绩一直落后,很着急。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bān shàng de chéngjì yìzhí luòhòu, hěn zháojí.
examples.english: His grades in class have always lagged behind, and he's anxious.

examples.hanzi: 我们的技术还落后别人一大截。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de jìshù hái luòhòu biéren yí dà jié.
examples.english: Our technology is still far behind others.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 帽, 帮: a belt of cloth with pieces hanging from it.
页 (head) — 页 is the head, as in 题, 顶, 颜; 领 is the neck and then to lead.
令 (lìng) — near sound — 领 is lǐng; 令 also sounds out 龄 líng and 铃 líng.

example.hanzi: 导游带领游客参观了故宫。
example.pinyin: Dǎoyóu dàilǐng yóukè cānguān le Gùgōng.
example.english: The guide led the tourists on a tour of the Forbidden City.
example.fact: The Forbidden City in Beijing was completed in 1420 during the Ming dynasty and served as the imperial palace for 24 emperors across the Ming and Qing dynasties. It contains 980 surviving buildings, making it the largest preserved palace complex in the world. The complex remained off-limits to ordinary citizens for nearly five centuries, giving rise to its English name.

examples.hanzi: 老师带领同学们唱起了校歌。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī dàilǐng tóngxuémen chàngqǐle xiàogē.
examples.english: The teacher led the students in singing the school song.

examples.hanzi: 他带领团队完成了这个重要的项目。
examples.pinyin: Tā dàilǐng tuánduì wánchéngle zhège zhòngyào de xiàngmù.
examples.english: He led the team to complete this important project.

meanings: to kidnap and force people into service

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.
丁 (dīng) — a nail seen from above; as a part it sounds out 钉 dīng, 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng, 灯 dēng.

example.hanzi: 拉丁语是许多欧洲语言的祖先。
example.pinyin: Lādīngyǔ shì xǔduō Ōuzhōu yǔyán de zǔxiān.
example.english: Latin is the ancestor of many European languages.
example.fact: Latin was the everyday language of the Roman Empire, which at its height in the 2nd century AD stretched from Britain to Egypt. As the empire fragmented, Latin evolved regionally into French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, and Romanian. Carl Linnaeus later chose Latin as the universal language for naming species in the 18th century, which is why scientific names like Homo sapiens remain in Latin today.

examples.hanzi: 这家书店有很多拉丁文的老书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā shūdiàn yǒu hěn duō Lādīngwén de lǎo shū.
examples.english: This bookstore has many old books in Latin.

examples.hanzi: 他的老师是个会说拉丁语的历史学家。
examples.pinyin: Tā de lǎoshī shì gè huì shuō Lādīngyǔ de lìshǐxuéjiā.
examples.english: His teacher is a historian who can speak Latin.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water — dyeing means soaking in a liquid.
木 (tree, plant) — 木 is the plant dye material, steeped in water to make colour.

example.hanzi: 感冒很容易传染给别人。
example.pinyin: Gǎnmào hěn róngyì chuánrǎn gěi biérén.
example.english: A cold is very easy to pass on to other people.
example.fact: Epidemiologists measure how contagious a disease is with a number called R0, the average number of people one sick person infects in a fully susceptible population. Measles has one of the highest known R0 values, between 12 and 18, meaning a single case can seed a dozen or more new infections before a vaccine campaign brings the outbreak under control. Ordinary seasonal influenza, by contrast, usually sits closer to an R0 of 1 to 2.

examples.hanzi: 小心点,别让你的感冒传染给孩子。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn diǎn, bié ràng nǐ de gǎnmào chuánrǎn gěi háizi.
examples.english: Be careful not to pass your cold on to the kids.

examples.hanzi: 这种病不会传染,你不用害怕。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìng bú huì chuánrǎn, nǐ bú yòng hàipà.
examples.english: This illness isn't contagious, so you needn't be afraid.

components.note: 童 (child) — as a sound unit, 童 also appears in 瞳 tóng and 撞 zhuàng; the character itself means child, as in 儿童.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.
车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.

example.hanzi: 那个国家的童子军大多是被绑架的儿童。
example.pinyin: Nàge guójiā de tóngzǐjūn dàduō shì bèi bǎngjià de értóng.
example.english: That country's child soldiers are mostly children who were kidnapped.
example.fact: The United Nations estimates that tens of thousands of children have been recruited into armed forces and groups in conflicts across more than a dozen countries in recent decades. In 2000, the UN adopted the Optional Protocol on the Involvement of Children in Armed Conflict, raising the minimum age for direct participation in hostilities to 18. Organizations like UNICEF run demobilization programs that combine trauma counseling with education and vocational training to help former child soldiers reintegrate into civilian life.

examples.hanzi: 我弟弟参加了童子军,周末常去露营。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìdi cānjiāle tóngzǐjūn, zhōumò cháng qù lùyíng.
examples.english: My younger brother joined the Scouts and often goes camping on weekends.

examples.hanzi: 童子军教会了孩子们怎么生火和打结。
examples.pinyin: Tóngzǐjūn jiàohuìle háizimen zěnme shēnghuǒ hé dǎjié.
examples.english: The Scouts taught the children how to light a fire and tie knots.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 住, 做.
木 (tree) — a person 亻 leaning on a tree 木: resting, hence 休息 rest and 退休 retire.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 假 is to borrow or fake, a person lending a false front.
叚 (jiǎ) sounds like 假; also in 暇 xiá and 霞 xiá.

example.hanzi: 我打算下个月休假去欧洲旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dǎsuàn xià ge yuè xiūjià qù Ōuzhōu lǚxíng.
example.english: I plan to take vacation next month to travel to Europe.
example.fact: The European Union's Working Time Directive requires member states to guarantee workers at least four weeks of paid annual leave, a floor that countries like France and Germany exceed. The United States, by contrast, has no federal law mandating any paid vacation at all, leaving it entirely up to employers. Studies by the U.S. Travel Association have found that despite this, many American workers leave unused vacation days on the table each year rather than taking the time off.

examples.hanzi: 下个星期我休假,哪儿也不去。
examples.pinyin: Xià gè xīngqī wǒ xiūjià, nǎr yě bú qù.
examples.english: I'm on leave next week and won't go anywhere.

examples.hanzi: 他在休假期间还是回了很多工作邮件。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài xiūjià qījiān háishi huíle hěn duō gōngzuò yóujiàn.
examples.english: He still answered lots of work emails while on vacation.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之) — marks movement and roads, as in 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; 逊 is yielding, giving way, as in 谦逊 humble.
孙 (sūn) — close sound: 逊 xùn. 孙 means grandchild.

example.hanzi: 他的成绩比我稍逊一筹。
example.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì bǐ wǒ shāo xùn yì chóu.
example.english: His grades are slightly below mine.
example.fact: 逊 means "inferior" or "modest": 逊色 (to be less impressive), 毫不逊色 (just as good), 谦逊 (humble), 出言不逊 (to speak rudely). It can also mean to abdicate: 逊位.

examples.hanzi: 他的英语不比你逊色。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Yīngyǔ bù bǐ nǐ xùnsè.
examples.english: His English is not inferior to yours.

examples.hanzi: 他很谦逊，从来不炫耀自己。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn qiānxùn, cónglái bù xuànyào zìjǐ.
examples.english: He is very modest and never shows off.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 撤 is to pull away. The right side matches old 徹 (now 彻 chè), which gave the sound.
離 (traditional) — 隹 (bird) plus 离 as sound (lí). 离 was an old name for a mythical beast, so the 'leave' sense comes from 離; 离 kept only the sound part.

example.hanzi: 台风来临前，居民被迫撤离沿海地区。
example.pinyin: Táifēng láilín qián, jūmín bèipò chèlí yánhǎi dìqū.
example.english: Before the typhoon arrived, residents were forced to evacuate the coastal area.
example.fact: After the Chernobyl nuclear disaster on April 26, 1986, the nearby city of Pripyat was not evacuated for almost 36 hours, even as radiation levels climbed. When the order finally came, roughly 49,000 residents were bussed out in under three hours, told only that the evacuation was temporary — most were never allowed to return, and the city remains an abandoned time capsule inside the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone today.

examples.hanzi: 火灾发生后,大楼里的人员迅速撤离。
examples.pinyin: Huǒzāi fāshēng hòu, dàlóu lǐ de rényuán xùnsù chèlí.
examples.english: After the fire broke out, the people in the building evacuated quickly.

examples.hanzi: 军队已经从那个城市撤离了。
examples.pinyin: Jūnduì yǐjīng cóng nàge chéngshì chèlí le.
examples.english: The army has already withdrawn from that city.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
要 (want, need) — oldest form shows hands at a waist: it meant "waist" (腰 yāo adds 月 flesh); "essential" followed.
纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads, as in 红, 经, 系: a pulled-tight cord. The top part is also in 坚 jiān (firm).

example.hanzi: 别担心，迟到一点不要紧。
example.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, chídào yìdiǎn bùyàojǐn.
example.english: Don't worry, it doesn't matter if you're a little late.
example.fact: Neuroscientists have found that simply being reassured by a trusted person can measurably dampen the brain's pain response, an effect documented in fMRI studies of the anterior cingulate cortex. This overlaps with the placebo effect, where inert treatments trigger real reductions in pain and anxiety simply because the recipient expects to feel better. The effect is strong enough that some hospitals now train staff in specific reassurance language to reduce patients' use of anesthesia during minor procedures.

examples.hanzi: 你摔了一跤,不要紧吧?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuāile yì jiāo, bú yàojǐn ba?
examples.english: You took a fall; it's nothing serious, right?

examples.hanzi: 这点小事不要紧,明天再说也行。
examples.pinyin: Zhè diǎn xiǎoshì bú yàojǐn, míngtiān zài shuō yě xíng.
examples.english: This little matter isn't urgent; it's fine to deal with it tomorrow.

components.note: 月 (moon) — in the oldest form the sun rises in the grass while the moon is still up: early morning. A court audience was held at dawn, hence cháo for court and dynasty.
鱼 (fish) — 鱼 is the fish radical, as in 鲨, 鲸; 鲜 pairs 鱼 with 羊 (sheep) — both freshly tasty foods, so fresh.

example.hanzi: 朝鲜与韩国之间的边境线是世界上戒备最森严的地区之一。
example.pinyin: Cháoxiǎn yǔ Hánguó zhījiān de biānjìngxiàn shì shìjiè shàng jièbèi zuì sēnyán de dìqū zhī yī.
example.english: The border between North Korea and South Korea is one of the most heavily guarded regions in the world.
example.fact: The Korean Demilitarized Zone is a 250-kilometer-long buffer strip roughly 4 kilometers wide that has separated North and South Korea since the 1953 armistice. Despite being lined with landmines, guard posts, and barbed wire, the near-total absence of human activity for seven decades has turned it into an accidental wildlife refuge, home to red-crowned cranes, Asiatic black bears, and possibly surviving populations of the Amur leopard.

examples.hanzi: 我在电视上看到了关于朝鲜的纪录片。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài diànshì shàng kàndàole guānyú Cháoxiǎn de jìlùpiàn.
examples.english: I saw a documentary about North Korea on TV.

examples.hanzi: 朝鲜族人爱吃冷面和泡菜。
examples.pinyin: Cháoxiǎnzú rén ài chī lěngmiàn hé pàocài.
examples.english: Korean ethnic people love eating cold noodles and kimchi.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — a picture of three peaks; as a radical it marks hills, as in 岛, 峰, 岸.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 我们爬到山上看日出。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen pá dào shānshàng kàn rìchū.
example.english: We climbed up the mountain to watch the sunrise.
example.fact: Air pressure drops steadily with altitude, which is why water boils at a lower temperature the higher up a mountain you go — at the summit of Mount Everest, water boils at around 70°C instead of 100°C, making it hard to cook food properly. This same pressure drop is why climbers above roughly 8,000 meters, a zone nicknamed the 'death zone,' need supplemental oxygen just to survive.

examples.hanzi: 山上的空气比城里清新多了。
examples.pinyin: Shān shàng de kōngqì bǐ chéng lǐ qīngxīn duō le.
examples.english: The air up in the mountains is much fresher than in the city.

examples.hanzi: 山上有一座很古老的寺庙。
examples.pinyin: Shān shàng yǒu yí zuò hěn gǔlǎo de sìmiào.
examples.english: There is a very old temple on the mountain.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
⺼ (flesh) — body parts, as in 脸 face, 脚 foot.
宛 (wǎn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 碗 wǎn and 婉 wǎn.

example.hanzi: 他打网球的时候不小心扭伤了手腕。
example.pinyin: Tā dǎ wǎngqiú de shíhou bù xiǎoxīn niǔshāng le shǒuwàn.
example.english: He accidentally sprained his wrist while playing tennis.
example.fact: The human wrist contains eight small carpal bones arranged in two rows, giving it an unusually wide range of motion compared to other joints. This complexity also makes it fragile: a fall onto an outstretched hand commonly causes a 'Colles' fracture' of the forearm bone near the wrist, one of the most frequent fractures seen in emergency rooms, especially in older adults with osteoporosis.

examples.hanzi: 他手腕上戴着一块旧手表。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǒuwàn shàng dàizhe yí kuài jiù shǒubiǎo.
examples.english: He wears an old watch on his wrist.

examples.hanzi: 这位经理很有手腕,能让大家都满意。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi jīnglǐ hěn yǒu shǒuwàn, néng ràng dàjiā dōu mǎnyì.
examples.english: This manager is very skillful at handling people and keeps everyone satisfied.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
彳 (step, 双人旁) — walking and journeys, as in 行 go, 往 toward, 得; 征 is a march or campaign.
正 (zhèng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 证 zhèng, 政 zhèng and 整 zhěng.

example.hanzi: 科学家根据化石的特征判断这是一种新物种。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā gēnjù huàshí de tèzhēng pànduàn zhè shì yì zhǒng xīn wùzhǒng.
example.english: Scientists determined from the fossil's characteristics that it was a new species.
example.fact: Paleontologists classify newly found fossils by comparing distinguishing physical traits against known specimens, a method called cladistics that groups organisms by shared derived characteristics rather than superficial resemblance. This approach overturned decades of assumptions, for instance revealing that birds are more closely related to certain dinosaurs like Velociraptor than crocodiles are to those same dinosaurs.

examples.hanzi: 这只鸟最明显的特征是红色的尾巴。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī niǎo zuì míngxiǎn de tèzhēng shì hóngsè de wěiba.
examples.english: The most obvious feature of this bird is its red tail.

examples.hanzi: 你能描述一下那个人的外貌特征吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng miáoshù yíxià nàge rén de wàimào tèzhēng ma?
examples.english: Can you describe that person's physical features?

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
习 (practice) — simplified from 習, a young bird 羽 flapping its wings again and again to learn to fly.

example.hanzi: 她暑假在一家科技公司实习。
example.pinyin: Tā shǔjià zài yì jiā kējì gōngsī shíxí.
example.english: She interned at a tech company over the summer.
example.fact: The modern internship traces back to medieval European guilds, where young apprentices spent years working under a master craftsman in exchange for training rather than pay. Germany's dual education system still formalizes this today: nearly half of German teenagers enter an Ausbildung, a structured multi-year apprenticeship combining paid on-the-job training with classroom study, before ever finishing what Americans would call a college degree.

examples.hanzi: 我明年大学毕业前要去医院实习。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngnián dàxué bìyè qián yào qù yīyuàn shíxí.
examples.english: Before I graduate from college next year, I have to do an internship at a hospital.

examples.hanzi: 学生们在工厂里实习了一个月。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen zài gōngchǎng lǐ shíxíle yí gè yuè.
examples.english: The students did a one-month internship in a factory.

components.note: 目 (eye) — eyes and seeing: 看 look, 眼 eye, 睛 eyeball; sleep is when the eyes close.
垂 (chuí, droop) hints at the sound and the image: drooping eyelids. Also in 锤 chuí.
目 (eye) — eyes and seeing, as in 看 look, 睡 sleep, 眼 eye; sleep is closing the eyes.
民 (mín) gives a close sound for mián.

example.hanzi: 良好的睡眠对身体健康非常重要。
example.pinyin: Liánghǎo de shuìmián duì shēntǐ jiànkāng fēicháng zhòngyào.
example.english: Good sleep is extremely important for physical health.
example.fact: During deep sleep, the brain's glymphatic system — discovered by researchers at the University of Rochester in 2012 — flushes out metabolic waste products, including beta-amyloid, a protein linked to Alzheimer's disease. Brain cells actually shrink slightly during sleep, widening the channels between them so cerebrospinal fluid can wash through more efficiently, essentially giving the brain a nightly cleaning cycle.

examples.hanzi: 我昨晚睡眠不好,今天没精神。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn shuìmián bù hǎo, jīntiān méi jīngshén.
examples.english: I didn't sleep well last night and have no energy today.

examples.hanzi: 手机进入睡眠模式后,屏幕就黑了。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī jìnrù shuìmián móshì hòu, píngmù jiù hēi le.
examples.english: After the phone enters sleep mode, the screen goes dark.

components.note: 页 (head) — marks the head and face, as in 顶, 题, 顺; 额 is the forehead, then an amount.
客 (kè) is a loose hint for é; 格 gé and 路 lù share it.

example.hanzi: 他的额头上有一道疤。
example.pinyin: Tā de étóu shàng yǒu yí dào bā.
example.english: He has a scar on his forehead.
example.fact: 额 is the forehead (额头) and also a fixed amount: 金额 (sum), 名额 (quota), 余额 (balance), 额外 (extra).

examples.hanzi: 这个月的开支超过了预算的额度。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè de kāizhī chāoguò le yùsuàn de édù.
examples.english: This month's spending exceeded the budget limit.

examples.hanzi: 今天报名的名额已经满了。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bàomíng de míng'é yǐjīng mǎn le.
examples.english: The places for today's registration are already full.

components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.
口 (mouth) — calling out; 夕 (evening) beside it: in the dark you cannot be seen, so you call your name.

example.hanzi: 很多网络作家不愿意公开自己的真名。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō wǎngluò zuòjiā bù yuànyì gōngkāi zìjǐ de zhēnmíng.
example.english: Many internet writers are unwilling to reveal their real names.
example.fact: The Portuguese poet Fernando Pessoa took the pseudonym further than almost any writer in history, inventing more than seventy 'heteronyms' — fully realized alternate authors with their own biographies, writing styles, and even astrological charts — rather than simply hiding his real name behind a single pen name. Samuel Clemens took a simpler route, borrowing the riverboat call 'mark twain,' meaning two fathoms of water depth, for his now far more famous byline.

examples.hanzi: 我只知道他的网名,不知道他的真名。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ zhīdào tā de wǎngmíng, bù zhīdào tā de zhēnmíng.
examples.english: I only know his online name, not his real name.

examples.hanzi: 这位演员用的是艺名,真名没人知道。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yǎnyuán yòng de shì yìmíng, zhēnmíng méi rén zhīdào.
examples.english: This actor uses a stage name, and nobody knows his real name.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 财, 费; 购 is to buy.
勾 (gōu) — near sound — 购 is gòu; 勾 also sounds out 构 gòu and 沟 gōu.
买 (simplified 買) — the old form shows a net 网 over a shell 贝 (money): netting goods, to buy. 卖 mài sell is built on 买.

example.hanzi: 消费者在购买商品前应该比较价格。
example.pinyin: Xiāofèizhě zài gòumǎi shāngpǐn qián yīnggāi bǐjiào jiàgé.
example.english: Consumers should compare prices before purchasing goods.
example.fact: The barcode, first scanned commercially on a pack of Wrigley's chewing gum in an Ohio supermarket in 1974, was designed to speed up checkout and track inventory automatically. Today the same UPC and QR-code systems process billions of purchases every day worldwide, and the original 1974 gum pack is now preserved in the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History.

examples.hanzi: 我想在网上购买一台新电脑。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zài wǎngshàng gòumǎi yì tái xīn diànnǎo.
examples.english: I'd like to buy a new computer online.

examples.hanzi: 购买这张票需要出示身份证。
examples.pinyin: Gòumǎi zhè zhāng piào xūyào chūshì shēnfènzhèng.
examples.english: You need to show your ID card to buy this ticket.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恐 is fear.
巩 (gǒng) is a near sound match (-ong).
忄 (heart) — a panicked heart; also in 怕 afraid, 急 anxious.
荒 (huāng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 谎 huǎng.

example.hanzi: 股市暴跌引发了投资者的恐慌。
example.pinyin: Gǔshì bàodiē yǐnfā le tóuzīzhě de kǒnghuāng.
example.english: The stock market crash triggered panic among investors.
example.fact: On October 24, 1929 — a day now remembered as 'Black Thursday' — nearly 13 million shares changed hands on the New York Stock Exchange as panicked investors rushed to sell, more than three times the normal volume. The resulting crash wiped out an estimated $30 billion in market value within days and helped trigger the decade-long Great Depression that followed.

examples.hanzi: 地震后,居民们陷入了恐慌。
examples.pinyin: Dìzhèn hòu, jūmínmen xiànrùle kǒnghuāng.
examples.english: After the earthquake, the residents fell into a panic.

examples.hanzi: 大家不要恐慌,保持冷静。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā bú yào kǒnghuāng, bǎochí lěngjìng.
examples.english: Everyone, don't panic; stay calm.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 科 first meant grading grain with a measure 斗, and then categories like 科学.
斗 (dipper) — 斗 is a measuring dipper, as in 斗 (a unit of grain).

example.hanzi: 他因为有前科而找工作很困难。
example.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi yǒu qiánkē ér zhǎo gōngzuò hěn kùnnán.
example.english: He has trouble finding work because he has a criminal record.
example.fact: Studies on hiring discrimination have found that job applicants with a criminal record receive roughly 50 percent fewer callbacks than identical applicants without one, even when they are equally qualified. This evidence helped drive the 'Ban the Box' movement in the United States, which has led more than 35 states to remove the criminal-history checkbox from initial job applications so candidates get evaluated on qualifications first.

examples.hanzi: 这个人以前有前科,警察一直盯着他。
examples.pinyin: Zhège rén yǐqián yǒu qiánkē, jǐngchá yìzhí dīngzhe tā.
examples.english: This man has a criminal record, and the police have kept an eye on him.

examples.hanzi: 有前科的人也应该有重新开始的机会。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu qiánkē de rén yě yīnggāi yǒu chóngxīn kāishǐ de jīhuì.
examples.english: People with a record should also have a chance to start over.

components.note: 心 (heart) — marks the mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 意; 忽 is a lapse of attention, hence neglect or suddenly.
勿 (wù) is a loose hint for hū; 物 wù shares it.
见 (see) — seeing and looking, as in 现, 觉, 看: 视 is to look.
礻 here is 示 (shì), the altar radical in 礼 and 神: in 视 it is the exact sound clue.

example.hanzi: 我们不应该忽视气候变化带来的影响。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen bù yīnggāi hūshì qìhòu biànhuà dàilái de yǐngxiǎng.
example.english: We should not neglect the effects brought by climate change.
example.fact: Since 1958, scientists atop Mauna Loa volcano in Hawaii have continuously measured atmospheric carbon dioxide levels, producing the now-famous 'Keeling Curve.' When measurements began, CO2 concentration stood at about 315 parts per million; it has since climbed past 420 parts per million, a level the planet had not seen in at least 800,000 years of ice-core records.

examples.hanzi: 他总是忽视老师给他的建议。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì hūshì lǎoshī gěi tā de jiànyì.
examples.english: He always overlooks the advice his teacher gives him.

examples.hanzi: 这个小问题不能被忽视。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo wèntí bù néng bèi hūshì.
examples.english: This small problem can't be ignored.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
十 (ten/cross) — the visible part; 升 once was a ladle measuring grain, then 'to rise'. The shape does not explain this. Memory aid: a ladle lifted high.

example.hanzi: 公司决定提升他为部门经理。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī juédìng tíshēng tā wéi bùmén jīnglǐ.
example.english: The company decided to promote him to department manager.
example.fact: In 1969, Canadian educator Laurence J. Peter coined the 'Peter Principle,' the satirical but widely studied observation that employees in a hierarchy tend to be promoted based on performance in their current role until they reach a position where they are no longer competent — and then stay there. A 2018 study analyzing sales-employee promotion data at over 200 U.S. firms found real statistical evidence supporting the idea: the best salespeople were often promoted into management roles where they performed worse than average.

examples.hanzi: 我学了一年英语,听力提升得很快。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xuéle yì nián Yīngyǔ, tīnglì tíshēng de hěn kuài.
examples.english: I've studied English for a year, and my listening has improved quickly.

examples.hanzi: 他因为工作出色,被提升为经理。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi gōngzuò chūsè, bèi tíshēng wéi jīnglǐ.
examples.english: He was promoted to manager because of his excellent work.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
广 (building, shelter) — the roof-and-wall frame, as in 店, 床, 度. Here it is mostly the outline of the old 應.
心 (heart) — hidden in the traditional 應, 'respond from the heart'; simplification dropped it. 应 is yīng (should) or yìng (respond).

example.hanzi: 这种门装有感应装置，人靠近就会自动打开。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng mén zhuāng yǒu gǎnyìng zhuāngzhì, rén kàojìn jiù huì zìdòng dǎkāi.
example.english: This kind of door has a sensor device that opens automatically when someone approaches.
example.fact: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831 by moving a magnet through a coil of wire and noticing it generated an electric current, even though the magnet and wire never touched. This single principle underlies nearly all modern electricity generation, from the giant turbines in power plants to the wireless charging pad that powers up a phone by induction alone.

examples.hanzi: 这个水龙头是感应式的,手一伸过去就出水。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shuǐlóngtóu shì gǎnyìng shì de, shǒu yì shēn guòqù jiù chūshuǐ.
examples.english: This faucet is sensor-based and water comes out as soon as you reach a hand over.

examples.hanzi: 手机的感应不太灵敏。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī de gǎnyìng bú tài língmǐn.
examples.english: The phone's sensor isn't very sensitive.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 挪 is shifting something by hand.
那 (nà) — close sound: 挪 nuó. 那 also sounds out 哪 nǎ and 娜 nuó.

example.hanzi: 请把椅子往旁边挪一下。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yǐzi wǎng pángbiān nuó yíxià.
example.english: Please move the chair over a bit.
example.fact: 挪 moves something a short distance: 挪动, 挪一挪. 挪用 means to misappropriate funds (挪用公款), and 挪窝 is colloquial for moving house. 挪威 is Norway.

examples.hanzi: 我想把沙发往窗户那边挪一挪。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bǎ shāfā wǎng chuānghu nàbiān nuó yi nuó.
examples.english: I want to move the sofa a little toward the window.

examples.hanzi: 你能不能挪个位置给我？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bu néng nuó ge wèizhi gěi wǒ?
examples.english: Could you shift over and make some room for me?

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — words and talk: 说, 话, 读; a spoken mistake or misunderstanding.
吴 (wú) gives the sound (wù, tone differs); same series 娱 yú and 虞 yú.

example.hanzi: 对不起，这是一个误会。
example.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, zhè shì yí ge wùhuì.
example.english: Sorry, this is a misunderstanding.
example.fact: 误 is a mistake or a harmful delay: 误会 (misunderstanding, the most common word), 错误 (error), 耽误 (to hold up), 误解, 失误 (a slip), 误导 (to mislead). It sounds more formal than 错.

examples.hanzi: 地铁出了问题，我们被耽误了半小时。
examples.pinyin: Dìtiě chū le wèntí, wǒmen bèi dānwu le bàn xiǎoshí.
examples.english: The subway had a problem and we were delayed by half an hour.

examples.hanzi: 这道题我做错了，是计算失误。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào tí wǒ zuò cuò le, shì jìsuàn shīwù.
examples.english: I got this question wrong because of a calculation mistake.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做; 任 is a duty a person bears.
壬 (rén) gives the same sound, different tone; also in 妊 rèn.

example.hanzi: 新任经理接手了前任留下的很多问题。
example.pinyin: Xīnrèn jīnglǐ jiēshǒu le qiánrèn liúxià de hěn duō wèntí.
example.english: The new manager inherited many problems left by his predecessor.
example.fact: In 1801, John Adams became the first U.S. president to hand power to a political rival, Thomas Jefferson, after losing a bitterly contested election — a peaceful transfer that was far from guaranteed to happen anywhere in the world at the time. Adams was so embittered by the loss that he skipped Jefferson's inauguration entirely, leaving Washington before dawn.

examples.hanzi: 我的前任同事现在在另一家公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de qiánrèn tóngshì xiànzài zài lìng yì jiā gōngsī gōngzuò.
examples.english: My former colleague now works at another company.

examples.hanzi: 他很少提起自己的前任。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn shǎo tíqǐ zìjǐ de qiánrèn.
examples.english: He seldom mentions his ex.

meanings: eager to do sth without delay

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking, roads and motion, as in 过 pass, 进 enter, 追 chase; 迫 is to press or drive someone on.
白 (bái) is a loose hint for pò; 拍 pāi and 泊 bó share the same part.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
及 (reach) — a hand 又 catching up with a person from behind: to reach, then and; seen in 以及, 及时.
彳 (step, left foot) — walking and roads: 行, 往, 很, 得; 待 is to go toward and wait on someone.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue; its family varies: 诗 shī, 持 chí, 特 tè, 等 děng.

example.hanzi: 孩子们迫不及待地想要打开圣诞礼物。
example.pinyin: Háizimen pòbùjídài de xiǎng yào dǎkāi Shèngdàn lǐwù.
example.english: The children couldn't wait to open their Christmas presents.
example.fact: Neuroscientist Wolfram Schultz's experiments on dopamine in the 1990s revealed that the brain's reward chemical spikes most sharply in anticipation of a reward, not upon receiving it — a discovery that reshaped how psychologists understand craving and motivation. This is part of why the wait for a gift, a text message, or a paycheck can feel more intensely emotional than the moment it actually arrives.

examples.hanzi: 我迫不及待想告诉你这个好消息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ pòbùjídài xiǎng gàosu nǐ zhège hǎo xiāoxi.
examples.english: I can't wait to tell you this good news.

examples.hanzi: 他迫不及待地打开了信。
examples.pinyin: Tā pòbùjídài de dǎkāile xìn.
examples.english: He eagerly opened the letter.

meanings: fig. original voice of a poet

components.note: 欠 (yawn, open mouth) — 欠 shows a person with an open mouth, as in 吹 blow, 欢 joyful; 歌 is the mouth opened in song.
哥 (gē) — same sound — 歌 is gē, just like 哥; 哥 means elder brother.
聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.

example.hanzi: 夜晚的公园里传来悠扬的歌声。
example.pinyin: Yèwǎn de gōngyuán lǐ chuánlái yōuyáng de gēshēng.
example.english: A melodious singing voice drifted through the park at night.
example.fact: Humpback whales compose songs that can last over 30 minutes and are sung in complex, repeating patterns that spread across entire ocean populations, with all males in a region often singing a similar version that slowly evolves over years — much like a cultural trend passed from whale to whale. Researchers still don't fully agree on why they sing, though mating display and long-distance communication across dozens of kilometers of ocean are leading theories.

examples.hanzi: 她的歌声很甜,大家都爱听。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gēshēng hěn tián, dàjiā dōu ài tīng.
examples.english: Her singing voice is sweet, and everyone loves to hear it.

examples.hanzi: 远处传来了孩子们的歌声。
examples.pinyin: Yuǎnchù chuánláile háizimen de gēshēng.
examples.english: The sound of children singing came from afar.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
虍 (tiger head) — the striped head and body of a tiger; also in 虑 lǜ, 虚 xū.

example.hanzi: 动物园里的老虎正在悠闲地散步。
example.pinyin: Dòngwùyuán lǐ de lǎohǔ zhèngzài yōuxián de sànbù.
example.english: The tiger at the zoo is leisurely taking a walk.
example.fact: Every tiger has a unique stripe pattern, much like a human fingerprint, and remarkably the stripes are visible even on a tiger's shaved skin, meaning the pattern is set in the skin itself rather than just the fur. Wild tiger populations have fallen by roughly 95 percent over the past century, from around 100,000 individuals in 1900 to fewer than 5,000 today, largely due to habitat loss and poaching.

examples.hanzi: 老虎是一种很危险的大型动物。
examples.pinyin: Lǎohǔ shì yì zhǒng hěn wēixiǎn de dàxíng dòngwù.
examples.english: The tiger is a very dangerous large animal.

examples.hanzi: 我属老虎,你属什么?
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shǔ lǎohǔ, nǐ shǔ shénme?
examples.english: I was born in the year of the tiger; what about you?

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 话 speech; 议 is to discuss.
义 (yì) sounds exactly like 议; same part in 仪 yí and 蚁 yǐ.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 议会将在下周投票决定这项法案。
example.pinyin: Yìhuì jiāng zài xià zhōu tóupiào juédìng zhè xiàng fǎ'àn.
example.english: Parliament will vote next week to decide on this bill.
example.fact: Iceland's Althing, founded in 930 AD at Þingvellir, is widely considered the oldest parliamentary institution still functioning today, roughly 1,000 years old. Early sessions were held outdoors on a natural rock formation that let a speaker's voice carry across the assembled crowd — an ancient acoustic trick long before microphones existed.

examples.hanzi: 议会通过了新的教育法。
examples.pinyin: Yìhuì tōngguòle xīn de jiàoyù fǎ.
examples.english: Parliament passed the new education law.

examples.hanzi: 他当选为议会的议员。
examples.pinyin: Tā dāngxuǎn wéi yìhuì de yìyuán.
examples.english: He was elected a member of parliament.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
火 (fire) — a picture of flames, and a component seen in 烧, 灯, 热 (as the dots 灬), 炒; fire radical for burning and heat.

example.hanzi: 森林里突然发生了一场大火。
example.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ tūrán fāshēng le yì chǎng dàhuǒ.
example.english: A large fire suddenly broke out in the forest.
example.fact: The 2019-2020 Australian bushfire season, nicknamed the 'Black Summer,' burned an estimated 18.6 million hectares — an area larger than the entire country of Syria — and was intense enough to generate its own thunderstorms, called pyrocumulonimbus clouds, that lofted smoke more than 15 kilometers into the stratosphere and circled the globe.

examples.hanzi: 这场大火烧了三个小时才被扑灭。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng dàhuǒ shāole sān gè xiǎoshí cái bèi pūmiè.
examples.english: This big fire burned for three hours before it was put out.

examples.hanzi: 大火过后,村子变成了一片废墟。
examples.pinyin: Dàhuǒ guòhòu, cūnzi biànchéngle yí piàn fèixū.
examples.english: After the great fire, the village turned into ruins.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a figure curled up gives the idea of rolling; 卷 sounds out 圈 quān, 拳 quán and 倦 juàn.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 他不小心卷入了一场政治丑闻。
example.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn juǎnrù le yì chǎng zhèngzhì chǒuwén.
example.english: He accidentally got drawn into a political scandal.
example.fact: The word 'scandal' ultimately traces back to the ancient Greek skandalon, meaning a trap or stumbling block set to trip someone up. The Watergate scandal of the early 1970s, named simply after the Washington, D.C. hotel where a break-in occurred, became so culturally dominant that the '-gate' suffix has since been attached to hundreds of unrelated controversies, from 'Deflategate' to 'Bridgegate.'

examples.hanzi: 我不想卷入你们之间的争吵。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng juǎnrù nǐmen zhījiān de zhēngchǎo.
examples.english: I don't want to get dragged into your quarrel.

examples.hanzi: 小船被卷入了大海的漩涡。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎochuán bèi juǎnrùle dàhǎi de xuánwō.
examples.english: The small boat was swept into the whirlpool of the sea.

components.note: 虫 (insect, creature) — small animals and insects, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake, 虾 shrimp: 蛋 is the egg of a creature.
虫 (insect, creature) — small animals and insects, as in 蚊 mosquito, 蛇 snake, 虾 shrimp: 蛋 is the egg of a creature.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了一下他的蛋蛋，说没有问题。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le yíxià tā de dàndàn, shuō méiyǒu wèntí.
example.english: The doctor examined his testicles and said there was no problem.
example.fact: Human testicles are held outside the main body cavity because sperm production works best at a temperature about 2-4°C cooler than core body temperature. The cremaster muscle can pull them closer to the body for warmth or let them hang lower to cool down, acting as a built-in thermostat that responds to ambient temperature within seconds.

examples.hanzi: 我家的小狗叫蛋蛋,特别可爱。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā de xiǎo gǒu jiào Dàndàn, tèbié kě'ài.
examples.english: Our puppy is called Dandan, and it's especially cute.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈叫他蛋蛋,是因为他小时候圆圆的。
examples.pinyin: Māma jiào tā Dàndàn, shì yīnwèi tā xiǎoshíhou yuányuán de.
examples.english: Mom calls him Dandan because he was round as a child.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — payment and loss, as in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
咅 (pōu) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 陪 péi and 培 péi.
亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做, 借; 偿 is to repay.
尝 (cháng) gives the sound exactly: 偿 cháng.

example.hanzi: 保险公司同意赔偿他的医疗费用。
example.pinyin: Bǎoxiǎn gōngsī tóngyì péicháng tā de yīliáo fèiyòng.
example.english: The insurance company agreed to compensate his medical expenses.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved in Babylon around 1754 BC, is one of the earliest known legal codes to formalize compensation for harm, prescribing specific payments or penalties depending on the victim's social status and the severity of the injury. Modern compensation law still echoes this idea of proportional restitution, though it has moved away from Hammurabi's more infamous 'eye for an eye' punishments.

examples.hanzi: 你弄坏了他的手机,应该赔偿。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ nònghuàile tā de shǒujī, yīnggāi péicháng.
examples.english: You broke his phone, so you should compensate him.

examples.hanzi: 航空公司赔偿了乘客的损失。
examples.pinyin: Hángkōng gōngsī péichángle chéngkè de sǔnshī.
examples.english: The airline compensated the passengers for their losses.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 游; 潜 is to dive under the water, hence hidden, as in 潜水.
水 (water) — a picture of flowing water; as a radical it appears as 氵 on the left (海, 河) or 水 at the bottom (泉, 冰).

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在假期去海边潜水。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài jiàqī qù hǎibiān qiánshuǐ.
example.english: He likes to go diving at the seaside during vacations.
example.fact: Free-diver Herbert Nitsch set the current world record in 2007 by descending to 214 meters on a single breath, a depth at which the human body experiences immense pressure changes in just a couple of minutes. Scuba divers going that deep with compressed air risk 'nitrogen narcosis,' a state resembling drunkenness caused by nitrogen dissolving into the bloodstream under pressure, which is why deep technical dives use special gas mixes instead of ordinary air.

examples.hanzi: 我们打算明年夏天去学潜水。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎsuàn míngnián xiàtiān qù xué qiánshuǐ.
examples.english: We plan to go learn to dive next summer.

examples.hanzi: 我平时在论坛上只看帖子,很少说话,就是潜水。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ píngshí zài lùntán shàng zhǐ kàn tiězi, hěn shǎo shuōhuà, jiùshì qiánshuǐ.
examples.english: I usually only read posts on the forum and rarely speak; I just lurk.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 吃, 叫; 咒 is a curse spoken aloud.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 语 is language and spoken words.
吾 (wú) — loose hint — 语 is yǔ; 吾 also sounds out 悟 wù.

example.hanzi: 巫师念了一段神秘的咒语。
example.pinyin: Wūshī niàn le yí duàn shénmì de zhòuyǔ.
example.english: The sorcerer recited a mysterious incantation.
example.fact: Archaeologists have recovered thousands of ancient Egyptian magical papyri containing spoken incantations meant to heal illness, ward off scorpions, or curse enemies, many written in a hybrid of Egyptian and Greek. Anthropologists studying ritual language today note that the rhythmic, repetitive structure common to spells and chants across unrelated cultures — from West African praise poetry to Tibetan mantras — may work partly by inducing a measurable calming effect on the nervous system, independent of any supernatural claim.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的巫师念着咒语,变出了一只兔子。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de wūshī niànzhe zhòuyǔ, biànchūle yì zhī tùzi.
examples.english: In the story, the wizard recited a spell and conjured up a rabbit.

examples.hanzi: 这个咒语好像对他一点用也没有。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zhòuyǔ hǎoxiàng duì tā yìdiǎn yòng yě méiyǒu.
examples.english: This spell doesn't seem to work on him at all.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and swimming, as in 河, 海, 泳: swimming and drifting.
斿 (yóu) gives the exact sound: a flag with streamers that floats freely.
舟 (boat) — ships and boats, as in 船 ship, 航 sail.
廷 (tíng) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 挺 tǐng and 庭 tíng.

example.hanzi: 富豪们喜欢在地中海驾驶游艇度假。
example.pinyin: Fùháomen xǐhuan zài Dìzhōnghǎi jiàshǐ yóutǐng dùjià.
example.english: Wealthy people like to cruise on yachts in the Mediterranean for vacation.
example.fact: The English word 'yacht' comes from the Dutch jaghtschip, literally 'hunt ship,' originally referring to small, fast vessels the Dutch navy used to pursue pirates and smugglers along shallow coastlines in the 16th century. When King Charles II returned from exile in the Netherlands in 1660, he brought the concept — and the word — back to England, where yachting quickly became a leisure pursuit of the aristocracy rather than a naval tactic.

examples.hanzi: 他们周末租了一艘游艇出海。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhōumò zūle yì sōu yóutǐng chūhǎi.
examples.english: They rented a yacht to go out to sea this weekend.

examples.hanzi: 码头上停着好几艘白色的游艇。
examples.pinyin: Mǎtou shàng tíngzhe hǎo jǐ sōu báisè de yóutǐng.
examples.english: Several white yachts were moored at the dock.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 marks thoughts and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感; 念 is to think of someone.
今 (jīn) — loose hint — 念 is niàn; 今 also sounds out 琴 qín and 含 hán, and means "now".
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 他心里突然冒出一个奇怪的念头。
example.pinyin: Tā xīnlǐ tūrán mào chū yí ge qíguài de niàntou.
example.english: A strange thought suddenly popped into his mind.
example.fact: A 2020 study by cognitive neuroscientists at Queen's University in Canada used fMRI brain-scanning patterns to estimate that the average person experiences roughly 6,000 distinct thoughts per day, a figure the researchers described as 'thought worms' — discrete bursts of neural activity that mark the transition from one idea to the next.

examples.hanzi: 我有个念头,想辞职去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu gè niàntou, xiǎng cízhí qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: I have an idea of quitting my job to travel.

examples.hanzi: 他打消了去国外读书的念头。
examples.pinyin: Tā dǎxiāole qù guówài dúshū de niàntou.
examples.english: He gave up the idea of studying abroad.

components.note: 用 (to use) — 甩 looks like 用 with the last stroke flicked out. Memory aid: use something up by flinging it away.
扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions — 掉 is to drop or lose hold.

example.hanzi: 她终于甩掉了那个不良习惯。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú shuǎidiào le nàge bùliáng xíguàn.
example.english: She finally got rid of that bad habit.
example.fact: MIT neuroscientist Ann Graybiel's research identified the basal ganglia as the brain region that encodes habits as automatic 'cue-routine-reward' loops, which is why habits can persist even after the original motivation disappears. Contrary to the popular claim that it takes 21 days to break a habit, a 2009 University College London study found the real average is closer to 66 days, with wide variation depending on the behavior and the person.

examples.hanzi: 我走得很快,终于甩掉了跟着我的小狗。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zǒu de hěn kuài, zhōngyú shuǎidiàole gēnzhe wǒ de xiǎogǒu.
examples.english: I walked fast and finally shook off the puppy that was following me.

examples.hanzi: 他想甩掉身上的泥巴,就用力抖了抖衣服。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng shuǎidiào shēnshang de níbā, jiù yònglì dǒule dǒu yīfu.
examples.english: He wanted to shake off the mud, so he shook his clothes hard.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants — medicine was made from herbs, as in 药 and 草.
约 (yuē) — near sound — 药 is yào; 约 also sounds out 钓 diào.
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 这家药店出售各种药品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā yàodiàn chūshòu gèzhǒng yàopǐn.
example.english: This pharmacy sells all kinds of medicines.
example.fact: Aspirin's active compound has roots in willow bark, which ancient Egyptian and Greek physicians used to relieve pain and fever thousands of years ago. Chemist Felix Hoffmann at the German company Bayer first synthesized a stable, less irritating version — acetylsalicylic acid — in 1897, and it remains one of the most widely used drugs in the world, with over 40,000 tons produced annually.

examples.hanzi: 这些药品要放在小孩拿不到的地方。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē yàopǐn yào fàng zài xiǎohái ná bú dào de dìfang.
examples.english: Keep these medicines where children can't reach them.

examples.hanzi: 进口药品需要通过检查才能销售。
examples.pinyin: Jìnkǒu yàopǐn xūyào tōngguò jiǎnchá cái néng xiāoshòu.
examples.english: Imported drugs must pass inspection before they can be sold.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun radical — dark is the lack of daylight; compare 明 bright, 晚 evening.
音 (yīn) — loose sound hint — 暗 is àn; 音 also sounds out 谙 ān.
乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).

example.hanzi: 那位国王在1914年遭到暗杀。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi guówáng zài 1914 nián zāodào ànshā.
example.english: That king was assassinated in 1914.
example.fact: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary was assassinated in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, by Gavrilo Princip, a 19-year-old Bosnian Serb nationalist. The assassination set off a diplomatic crisis that escalated within weeks into World War I, ultimately drawing in over 30 countries and killing more than 16 million people.

examples.hanzi: 这部老电影讲的是一次暗杀行动。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù lǎo diànyǐng jiǎng de shì yí cì ànshā xíngdòng.
examples.english: This old film is about an assassination plot.

examples.hanzi: 历史书里写了那位首相被暗杀的经过。
examples.pinyin: Lìshǐshū lǐ xiěle nà wèi shǒuxiàng bèi ànshā de jīngguò.
examples.english: The history book tells how that prime minister was assassinated.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort, as in 助, 男, 努: handling things takes effort. The two dots stand in for 辡 of the traditional 辦.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 他去政府部门办事，排了很长时间的队。
example.pinyin: Tā qù zhèngfǔ bùmén bànshì, pái le hěn cháng shíjiān de duì.
example.english: He went to a government department to handle some business and waited in a long line.
example.fact: In 1955, British historian C. Northcote Parkinson observed what became known as 'Parkinson's Law of bureaucracy': that administrative staff in an organization tend to multiply at a fixed rate of about 5-7 percent per year regardless of the actual amount of work to be done. Estonia has taken the opposite approach since the 2000s, digitizing nearly all government services so that citizens can file taxes, vote, and register a business online in minutes rather than visiting an office in person.

examples.hanzi: 你去银行办事,别忘了带身份证。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ qù yínháng bànshì, bié wàngle dài shēnfènzhèng.
examples.english: When you go to the bank to take care of business, don't forget your ID card.

examples.hanzi: 他办事很认真,大家都信任他。
examples.pinyin: Tā bànshì hěn rènzhēn, dàjiā dōu xìnrèn tā.
examples.english: He works very conscientiously, and everyone trusts him.

components.note: 异 (simplified 異) — means different or strange; its yì sound also appears in 翼 yì (wing).
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 情, 快, 怕; 性 is the inner nature of a thing.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint; also in 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 青春期的孩子开始对异性产生好感。
example.pinyin: Qīngchūnqī de háizi kāishǐ duì yìxìng chǎnshēng hǎogǎn.
example.english: Children in puberty begin to develop feelings for the opposite sex.
example.fact: Puberty begins when the hypothalamus starts releasing gonadotropin-releasing hormone in pulses, which in turn signals the pituitary gland to release hormones that trigger the ovaries or testes to mature. The average onset age has been dropping globally for over a century — in the mid-1800s the average girl had her first period around age 17, while today the global average is closer to 12, a shift researchers link partly to improved nutrition.

examples.hanzi: 这个班的男生和女生一起做游戏,没有异性的隔阂。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bān de nánshēng hé nǚshēng yìqǐ zuò yóuxì, méiyǒu yìxìng de gémó.
examples.english: Boys and girls in this class play together without any barrier between the sexes.

examples.hanzi: 同性相斥,异性相吸,这是一种说法。
examples.pinyin: Tóngxìng xiāng chì, yìxìng xiāng xī, zhè shì yì zhǒng shuōfǎ.
examples.english: Same sexes repel and opposite sexes attract; that's one saying.
